'''Edward Adam Davis''' (born June 5, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played 12 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played high school basketball at [[Benedictine High School (Richmond, Virginia)|Benedictine High School]] in [[Richmond, Virginia]]. He is the son of former NBA player [[Terry Davis (basketball)|Terry Davis]].<ref name="tarheelblue.cstv.com">{{Cite web |url=http://www.goheels.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=3350&ATCLID=205673998 |title=Player Bio: Ed Davis |access-date=October 28, 2013 |archive-date=March 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160314134902/http://www.goheels.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205673998&DB_OEM_ID=3350 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was selected with the 13th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]] by the [[Toronto Raptors]].

==High school career==
Davis spent his first two years of high school playing basketball at [[Hanover High School (Mechanicsville, Virginia)|Hanover High School]] in [[Mechanicsville, Virginia]] before transferring to [[Benedictine High School (Richmond, Virginia)|Benedictine High School]] in [[Richmond, Virginia]]. There, he led Benedictine to two state championships while averaging 22 points, 14 rebounds and 7 blocks as a senior.<ref name="tarheelblue.cstv.com"/> He accompanied future Tar Heel teammates [[Tyler Zeller]] and [[Larry Drew II]] in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]] and was selected to the Jordan Brand All-American Team. He was named Mr. Basketball of Virginia in 2008, which is given to Virginia's best high school basketball player. He also received recognition as the co-player of the year in 2007.<ref name="tarheelblue.cstv.com"/>

Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Davis was listed as the No. 4 power forward and the No. 15 player in the nation in 2008.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Ed-Davis-48045;_ylt=AtcuSzLHkFp0bnrXCfPFavVGPZB4 Ed Davis Recruiting Profile]</ref>

==College career==
Davis played in every game during the 2008–09 season, while starting in two of them. He averaged 6.7 points, 7.0 rebounds, and 18.8 minutes per game in his first season with the Tar Heels. Davis also led the team with 65 blocks with an average of 1.7 per game. In North Carolina's six wins during the [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2009 NCAA tournament]], Davis averaged 8.2 points and 5.5 rebounds. In the [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|2009 NCAA championship game]], Davis came off the bench to score 11 points and grab a team-high 8 rebounds, helping the Tar Heels to an 89–72 win over [[Michigan State]].<ref name="sportsillustrated.cnn.com">{{cite news| url=http://www.goheels.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=3350&ATCLID=205485042 | work=GoHeels.com | title=Ed Davis To Return To UNC For Sophomore Season | date=April 12, 2009 |access-date=April 12, 2009}}</ref> Davis was also named to the 2009 All-Freshman Team and was co-recipient of the team's Most Improved Player award.<ref name="tarheelblue.cstv.com"/>

In April 2009, Davis announced he would return to North Carolina after his freshman year instead of declaring for the [[NBA draft]].<ref name="sportsillustrated.cnn.com"/> In February 2010, he suffered a broken wrist in a loss to Duke, which effectively ended his season. In 2009–10, he played 23 games, averaging 13.4 points, 9.6 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 2.8 blocks per game.<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/ed-davis-1.html Ed Davis Stats] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714124404/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/ed-davis-1.html |date=July 14, 2014 }}</ref> Davis was seen as a projected top three pick in the [[2009 NBA draft]] had he declared .<ref>{{Cite web|last=Behcet|first=Pompaci|title=NBA Draft Results: Toronto Raptors Pick Ed Davis at 13th|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/411102-nba-draft-toronto-raptors-pick-ed-davis-at-13th|access-date=2022-02-14|website=Bleacher Report|language=en}}</ref>

In April 2010, Davis declared for the NBA draft, foregoing his final two years of college eligibility.<ref>[http://www.wralsportsfan.com/unc/story/7405119/ North Carolina’s Ed Davis declares for NBA draft]</ref> He signed with [[sports agent]] [[Rob Pelinka]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsbusinessdaily.com/Daily/Issues/2010/05/Issue-166/Sports-Industrialists/Pelinka-Signs-Two-Potential-NBA-Lottery-Picks-Falk-Inks-Monroe.aspx|title=Pelinka Signs Two Potential NBA Lottery Picks; Falk Inks Monroe|access-date=May 13, 2010|date=May 11, 2010|work=SportsBusiness Daily.com|author=Mullen, Liz}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Toronto Raptors (2010–2013)===
[[File:Ed Davis Raptors (cropped).jpg|upright|thumb|Davis with the [[Toronto Raptors]] in 2012]]
Davis in the [[2009 NBA draft]] was seen as a projected top three pick .<ref name="sportsillustrated.cnn.com" /> Davis was selected by the [[Toronto Raptors]] with the 13th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. On July 6, 2010, he signed with the Raptors.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/davis_signs_pr070610.html Raptors Sign First-Round Pick Ed Davis]</ref> After a month with the Raptors, Davis was assigned to the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Raptors' rookie Davis to begin rehab stint|website=Sportsnet.com|agency=The Canadian Press|date=November 22, 2010|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/raptors-davis-2/|access-date=January 21, 2020}}</ref> On November 29, 2010, Davis was recalled by the Raptors.<ref>{{cite news|title=Raptors recall Ed Davis|work=The Globe and Mail|date=November 29, 2010|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/basketball/raptors-recall-ed-davis/article1316041/|access-date=January 21, 2020}}</ref> On December 1, 2010, he made his NBA debut against the Washington Wizards, recording 11 points, 6 rebounds, and 2 blocks. On April 5, 2011, Davis recorded a career-high 22 points against the New York Knicks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ed Davis 2010–11 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/davised01/gamelog/2011|access-date=January 21, 2020}}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2013–2014)===
On January 30, 2013, Davis was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], along with [[Tayshaun Prince]] and [[Austin Daye]] of the [[Detroit Pistons]], in a three team deal that also sent teammate [[José Calderón (basketball)|José Calderón]] to the Pistons, and [[Rudy Gay]] and [[Hamed Haddadi]] of the Grizzlies to the Raptors.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-tayshaun-prince-austin-daye-ed-davis-2013-draft-pick-130130|title=Grizzlies acquire Tayshaun Prince, Austin Daye, Ed Davis and 2013 second round draft pick in three-team deal|work=NBA.com|date=January 30, 2013|access-date=January 30, 2013}}</ref>

On June 30, 2014, the Grizzlies declined the opportunity to tender a qualifying offer to Davis, making him an unrestricted free agent.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-elect-no-offer-davis-140630 Grizzlies elect not to extend qualifying offer to Ed Davis; Team keeps options open]</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2014–2015)===
On July 23, 2014, Davis signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and played 79 games during the season averaging 8.3 points 7.6 rebounds and 1.2 rebounds with a season high points of 20.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lakers Sign Ed Davis |date=July 23, 2014 |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140723eddavis |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140810220532/http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/140723eddavis?cid=TW |archive-date=August 10, 2014 |url-status=dead |access-date=July 23, 2014 }}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2015–2018)===
On July 9, 2015, Davis signed a three-year, $20 million contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Forward Ed Davis|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-forward-ed-davis|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2015|access-date=July 13, 2015}}</ref><ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources--ed-davis-agrees-to--20-million-deal-with-trail-blazers-190056225.html Sources: Ed Davis agrees to $20 million deal with Trail Blazers]</ref> On November 20, 2015, he recorded 17 points and 15 rebounds in a 102–91 win over the Los Angeles Clippers. His 15 rebounds included a career-high 10 offensive rebounds, the most for a Blazer since [[Greg Oden]] had 10 in December 2009. He also became the first Blazers player to have at least 15 points and 15 rebounds off the bench since [[Travis Outlaw]] in 2006.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151120/LACPOR/gameinfo.html |title=Blazers snap 7-game skid with 102-91 win over Clippers |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 21, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180513193243/http://www.nba.com/games/20151120/LACPOR/gameinfo.html |archive-date=May 13, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On March 1, 2017, Davis was ruled out for the rest of the 2016–17 season after requiring arthroscopic surgery on his left shoulder to repair an injured labrum.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/article/2017/03/01/portland-trail-blazers-ed-davis-arthroscopic-surgery-left-shoulder Trail Blazers' Ed Davis to miss rest of season after surgery]</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2018–2019)===
[[File:Eddavis2019.jpg|thumb|upright|Davis takes a shot with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in 2019]]
On July 23, 2018, Davis signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]]. Davis only missed one game during the season and he averaged a low 5.8 points and had more rebounds than points with 8.6 rebounds, with only 0.8 a game. His season-high single-game point total was 17, and his rebounds were only one less with 16 .<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2018/07/23/brooklyn-nets-sign-ed-davis|title=BROOKLYN NETS SIGN ED DAVIS|work=NBA.com|date=July 23, 2018|access-date=July 23, 2018}}</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2019–2020)===
On July 20, 2019, Davis signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jazz Sign Ed Davis, Jeff Green and Emmanuel Mudiay|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/jazz-sign-davis-green-and-mudiay|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 20, 2019|date=July 20, 2019}}</ref> On November 2, 2019, the [[Utah Jazz]] announced that Davis suffered from a fractured left fibula during a seasons game vs. the [[Sacramento Kings]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings knock off Jazz 102-101 to end 5-game winless streak|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160717|date=November 2, 2019|website=ESPN.com|access-date=November 2, 2019}}</ref> and was expected to be sidelined for about four weeks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ed Davis injury update|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/ed-davis-injury-update|date=November 2, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 2, 2019}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2020–2021)===
On November 23, 2020, Davis was traded to the [[New York Knicks]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Team sends Ed Davis and future picks to New York |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/team-sends-ed-davis-and-future-picks-new-york |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 24, 2020 |date=November 23, 2020}}</ref> and on November 24 he was traded once again, this time to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Ed Davis From New York |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-ed-davis-new-york |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 24, 2020 |date=November 24, 2020}}</ref>

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2021–2022)===
On October 13, 2021, Davis signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref name="DavisJames">{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign Ed Davis|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/davis-signing-211013|website=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}}</ref>

=== Mets de Guaynabo (2023) ===
On February 4, 2023, Davis signed with [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN).<ref>{{Cite news |title=Ed Davis joins Mets de Guaynabo |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/ed-davis-joins-mets-de-guaynabo/ |access-date=February 26, 2023 |website=Sportando|date=February 4, 2023 |last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref> He was released by the team on April 10.

==Personal life==
Davis is the son of Angela Jones and [[Terry Davis (basketball)|Terry Davis]].<ref name="tarheelblue.cstv.com"/>

On June 29, 2026, Davis was indicted on sports gambling charges by federal prosecutors at the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York. <ref>{{cite news |last1=Charania |first1=Shams |last2=Purdum |first2=David |title=Ex-NBA players Malik Beasley, Ed Davis indicted in gambling case |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49215856/former-nba-players-malik-beasley-ed-davis-indicted-gambling-case |access-date=30 June 2026 |work=ESPN |date=29 June 2026}}</ref>
